[u]Discussions With The Government of Tirakan Regarding Pan-Shamatine Cooperation, Fighting Terrorism, a Baladullahan-Tirakan Trade Agreement and Decolonization of the Shamats[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [/i]

Over the past few days, the Baladullahan delegation to Greater Tirakan which includes Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi, Foreign Minister Abdoul Mahonomayi, Defense Minister Musa al-Yahudiyyah, met with Premier Arlan Vos and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Tirakan to discuss cooperation in the fields of trade, diplomacy, trade, opposition to colonialism, and fighting against terrorism. Sultan Masud and Premier Vos are both adamant defenders of national sovereignty, regional cooperation and military collaboration, and the importance of fighting terrorism and cross-border criminal activity.

The Baladullah-Tirakan Trade Agreement (BTTA) was developed through consultation between the ATK and the Tiraki side, and goes as follows:

[b][u]Baladullah-Tirakan Trade Agreement[/u][/b]

For the mutual benefit of Baladullah and Tirakan, this trade agreement, which will also be known by its acronym BTTA, has been developed and approved by the governments of Baladullah and Tirakan. God willing, this will bring great benefits to both of our nations.

Article I. Neither party will impose tariffs of more than 5%, and the general expectation is that there will be no tariffs imposed by either side unless absolutely necessary to protect a vital domestic industry. Prices will be set to be as fair as possible, and linked to market values.

Article II. Enterprises partially or fully funded by FDI (foreign direct investment) will pay 5% less taxes, and both sides will take necessary measures to facilitate the quick and efficient establishment of FDI funded enterprises through giving them priority in their regulatory systems.

Article III. Customs duties will be reduced by 5-10% by both sides.

Article IV. Both parties agree to sell resources and commodities they produce in large quantities to one another at a fixed sum, namely steel, copper, and gas. 

[It should be noted by Tirakan that Baladullah has a fully socialist economy, however, and we also do not allow the sale of alcohol, drugs, prngraphy, or media that mocks or lampoons Islam, Christianity, Judaism, Zoroastrianism, or Druze religion. All Tiraki enterprises in Baladullah must consent to having mandatory unions and workers delegates that participate in the operation and management of their enterprises]
-
Alhamdullilah, the negotiations between us and our brothers in Tirakan went very well, in my assessment. We are dedicated to the principles of the rule of law in a constitutional framework, battling extremism and terrorists, religious freedom, and the need to oppose colonialism and hegemonism around the world. In shaa Allah this is the beginning of a solid and successful partnership between Baladullah and Tirakan. -Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi

[Spoiler=Phinakha vs Delareaux]The match begins of the fourth matchday with a competitive match up between Phinakha and Delareaux, the game kicks off with high tensions from the start, aggressive play, fouls and arguing. In the 12th minute, Delareaux striker Kerador Yelmatai receives a ball from the right edge of the box and shoots it, it goes beautifully in the net with the opening goal of Matchday 4 in favor for Delareaux. Just 14 minutes later, Phinakha's attacking midfielder Lionel F'ressi gets awarded a penalty from a harsh foul in the box, He strikes it gracefully in the bottom left corner to seal the goal for Phinakha. And it was all for Phinakha's favor after, with Phinakha scoring two more goals to make it 3-1. In the second half, Delareaux looked more determined than ever. With Kerador Yelmatai scoring two more goals to mark his hattrick and making it 3-3 again for Delareaux, just in the 78th minute, Delareaux midfielder Erbenar Javörin, by a header from a corner kick. In the 88th minute, Delareaux gets one more goal to seal the 3-5 victory, an own goal by K'bassa Jarkpoor.

[spoiler=[b]Starbound RP: Prepare for War[/b]]

[b]9th January 2167 - Aktus Sphere - Korrin - Korr City[/b]

Vissarius' eyes slowly twitched closed as he barely managed to stay awake during the meeting, his mind dozing off while the Korrin Assembly discussed boring topics like the economy or infrastructure, their constant throwing of jargon words confusing Vissarius even more with each minute. His fingers ran across the cold metallic table with his head tilted down and resting on his left hand; he sighed as even more ministers and corporate representatives blabbered on about some margins. His father sat stoic next to him, his gaze fixated on the diagrams presented in the middle of the table.

Zytan sat at the centre of the room with a subtle smile on his face, and as the last minister finished their presentation and sat back down, he would clear his throat. He took a moment to shuffle through some paperwork, skimming through the agenda of the day and what he actually wanted to discuss, all mouths shut as people dared not make any noise while Zytan was deep in thought.

[i]"Well then, it appears we are finished with matters of the economy."[/i] Zytan said as he looked up at the rest of the assembly and slid away the papers. "Let's now move onto the matter of the military."

Vissarius' eyes shot wide open at the mention of the military and he leaned back, puffing up his chest and attempting to mimic his father's stoic position, arms crossed together.

[i]"It appears the Federation does not plan on seeking peace. The High Council has called for mobilisation and an offensive against us; they are looking to bring all the breakaway colonies back into their greedy hands. Our hopes for a bloodless independence are out of the window, and now we must plan to give the Federation the most decisive defeat. Korrin will not seek any peace other than total victory over the corrupt Federation forces."[/i] Zytan said as he folded his hands in front of his face, eyes gazing at the military officials in the assembly.

[i]"As you may know, Chancellor, Rosenmarkke has publicly stated that they support our self-determination and will not include themselves in offensive action against Korrin. That makes things simpler for us: one less nation to worry about and a potential partner. We must use this to our advantage. If we can somehow convince Rosenmarkke to leave the Federation, or perhaps align with them during our operation against Erene, we'll have an easier time during our invasion."[/i] Minister of Foreign Affairs Qutar Magrek spoke up.

[i]"Receiving recognition from Rosenmarkke is great news for us, however we must focus on assembling the Spacenoid coalition. Our economy may be able to support a war against the Federation, but if it is prolonged, then we will face food and water shortages. We must reach out to Ilynis and Zeonia for their participation in our invasion."[/i] Admiral Ascanius Vulkrim replied loudly.

[i]"If water is a concern, then let us dispatch a force towards Tellus. The local government is still aligned with the Federation, and if we can secure the moon's water, then that's one less thing to worry about. If not Tellus then trade with Hyperborea will work too."[/i] Captain Noa Chiram interjected.

Ascanius nodded. [i]"The Federation may use Tellus to launch an attack against us. A small naval group should be enough to tame the ice world; water is necessary if we wish to win. Relying on Hyperborean water is logistically difficult, and if Tellus answers the Federation's call they can intercept our cargo ships."[/i]

[i]"Then what about Aceldama and Palleon?"[/i] Asks Admiral Virren Kaifferon, raising his hand to get Zytan's attention. [i]"If the Federation manages to have those colonies mobilise against us, we'll have to spread our warship across two fronts. But the problem is that moving forces towards those two colonies will mean less for our invasion, and stalling our invasion just to secure Aktus would be playing into the Federation's hands."
[/i]
[i]"Aceldama and Palleon aren't in the hands of the Federation anymore. They too remember what the Federation has done against them; if we reach out, we may secure additional forces for our invasion. Let's give them an offer to join our coalition, assuring them that the defeat of Federation forces is the best course for their security."[/i] Replied Magrek with a large smile, leaning back in his chair as he eyed Virren.

[i]"So what then! We just sit in Aktus and wait for reinforcements from the other Spacenoids? What's to say Aceldama will actually join, or how long will it take for Zeonia to gather a force?"[/i] Vissarius interrupted by standing up and shouting to the assembly. [i]"The Federation is a slow beast, let us take the initiative while we can!"[/i]

[i]"The problem is we don't know the strength of the Federation. Currently only two nations have answered their call for war, but we may see more of them arrive to fight. Rushing into battle may result in us suffering a defeat."[/i] Ascanius replied.

[i]"Besides, our naval doctrine is designed around battle in Kartovsky Range. If we abandon this advantage and are forced to fight in deep space, then the Federation will have an easier time. We should gather information and let them come to us; we know the area and our expertise in Kartovsky warfare will decimate whatever fleet they send to us."[/i] Virren replied to his son, stern and professional, with every word emanating his strength.

[i]"And if they don't? All I need is my destroyer and a few frigates; they might try and manoeuvre to Aceldama, or their forces will be scattered. The Belt of Tears is a dangerous passage; if I can deal damage before they even reach the Sphere of Aktus, then our forces will sweep them without trouble. Hell, if it's a large force, I could lure them towards Korrin where we have an advantage."[/i]

Zytan nodded. [i]"Vissarius is right. If we sit here then the Federation will simply build up and overwhelm us. We need to put pressure on them, a strike fleet to patrol Mastodon and destroy their logistics will do enough to force some sort of response."[/i]

[i]"While I'm not against any probing attacks towards Erene, I am worried that this strike force may not have the capacity to engage effectively. Do we have any Comet-class watching the sectors?"[/i] Virren asked, his head turning to look at his son then quickly spinning back to face Zytan.

[i]"Ay. [b]KN I See You[/b] is currently performing reconnaissance; if they spot anything Vissarius would know. Let the boy have at it, perhaps a raid on Mastodon would do us good to secure food areas. That would solve the problem of prolonged war and give us a checkpoint to Erene."[/i] Noa Chiram chimed in.

[i]"Well then..."[/i] Zytan stood up, followed by the rest of the assembly. [i]"We should secure water, a small fleet to Tellus and another towards Aceldama just in case. If Vissarius is up for it, I will approve for him to set forth, let him see and prod at the Federation's frontier for any weakness, though a retreat back to Korrin is most advised should a stronger force be seen." Zytan sighed, a few droplets of sweat forming on his forehead. "Let us continue the hard work, and soon we shall enjoy our independence in peace. Sieg Korrin!"[/i][/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Incident at Whitney[/b]]

[b]Five miles north of Whitney, Province of Whitney[/b]

Upon receiving reports from the Hamilton Radar Station of the situation in the skies, the surrounding provinces perked up their atmospheric defenses to deal with the threat. However, upon witnessing the ship release a shuttle onto the moon, the unfolding events concerning the spacecraft gave attention to the military, who were now very intrigued in the unfolding situation. While unable to prevent the shuttle from reaching Aceldama, the radar stations were able to observe and pinpoint its trajectory and landing location, determining that it was headed for Whitney, a city easily visible from outer space.

~ ~ ~

The entrance of Frame 167 came sudden and quick, shooting down through the air at breakneck speed. When Frame 167 hit the earth, it conjured a powerful force in the ground, sending dust flying and rocks tumbling over, of which there were no witnesses to marvel. Upon landing, the mech slowly stood back up and looked straight, back facing the bright rays of the Sun. The driver within quickly paused to inspect his mech for damage. Once concluding that everything worked fine, Frame 167 turned on its boosters and began to hover around the badlands of Aceldama for signs of human settlement.

It didnt take very long. About 20 minutes into the operation, Frame 167 spotted about a dozen buildings in the distance. Upon inspection, it appeared to be a mining facility, laden with humans, robots and valuable infrastructure alike. Frame 167 saw no trace of military activity within the mining encampment, nor any defensible positions within the facility. A stunning target indeed, it thought. The mechs boosters flared with power and its plasma rifle was armed in preparation.

~ ~ ~

The miners never saw it coming. A few crewmen reported seeing something odd in the distance, but they were not nearly as calculating nor caring as the men in Hamilton Radar Station. And then, all of a sudden, a metal object- no, machine- was zooming towards the facility. A number of brave souls ran to ring the alarm, but it was too late. Within seconds, the giant mech, oddly with no markings for identification, began firing upon the encampment. A few valiant miners threw their wrenches and shovels at the mech, but these were scratches, if even, on the mech. The mech hoisted its shield and rammed it against a building, bursting through its walls and wreaking havoc upon the unsuspecting facility.

Luckily, for the inhabitants of the mining community, Aceldix had been watching over them, and had guessed with solid accuracy where the shuttle from earlier had landed. The mech, in a rampage to try out its polished rocket launchers, saw out of the corner of its eye a large, dark figure in the sky. It suddenly hit her: retribution was quickly approaching. She thus made it her goal to cause as much destruction as possible; just follow the orders, use everything in the arsenal. Minutes later, help arrived in the form of tanks and armored cars. 

Aceldix drew first blood, as a tank fired an explosive shell at the mech. Frame 167 quickly raised her shield, blocking the attack but staggering her in the process; she had reacted too fast and without confidence behind her step. Frame 167 wasted no time, as she fired rocket launchers at the armored battalion. This mech was armed to the teeth, the Aceldixans thought. Whose robot is this? Battle soon raged on, between the mysterious mech from the unnamed carrier and the defensive forces of Aceldix.

Much time passed, and Frame 167 was beginning to take heavy damage. The Aceldixans were much more numerous in number than previously thought. In the goal to cause as much damage as possible, Frame 167 launched a salvo of rockets from her shoulders before turning 180 degrees and attempting an escape from the ground-based vehicles. One of the tanks would fire a desperate shot at the mech to try and prevent its escape.

Lucky hit. And a mighty one at that.

The mech suddenly saw its own arm mangled and critical systems within heavily damaged. The mech hit the ground at tremendous force, rattling the very earth around. The armored vehicles were initially very quiet before maneuvering out of the mining grounds and moving towards the mech. But upon reaching it, everything seemed off about it.

"Corporal, are you ready?"

"Yes, Sergeant." Hardwick aims his rifle at the doorknob.

"OK then. Three, two, one... NOW!"

He fires the gun, blowing the knob to smithereens. Hardwick then kicks the busted door out of the way, and throws a flashbang into the room before ducking out of the way. Once the flashbang explodes, he leads the team of soldiers in, firing at anyone who dares oppose them on their mission. They have to execute this mission as quickly and as stealthily as possible - their man of the hour has a reputation for making dramatic escapes, most often by blowing up his meth lab, and they do not want a repeat of the previous mission where he did exactly that.

The lab is cleared in two minutes, leaving them only 25 minutes to find and exterminate their target, Ryder Brooke. They begin to scan the area, looking for any evidence that he may be or was in the building.

"Alpha-1, over there." One of the privates gesture at a door in the lab. "That has to be Brooke's office."

"Good catch, Alpha-3." Hardwick taps Sergeant Mike on the back and points. The Sergeant nods, and leads the team to the door. The rest of them congregate to one side of the doorway, while the Sergeant stands in front of it and prepares to blow the door to pieces. Hardwick pulls out another flashbang, and removes the pin, ready to throw it into the room on the Sergeant's command.

"Ready?"

"Three. Two. O-"

A bullet punches its way through the door and embeds itself in Sergeant Mike's head. For a few moments afterward, everything falls dead silent. Then, with a weak groan and an echoing thump, the Sergeant falls backward, and a pool of blood forms below his stricken corpse.

"Sarge!" Some of the privates immediately scramble to help their fallen comrade. Hardwick stands in shock, trying to understand what has just unfolded before his eyes.

As the reality of the situation dawns upon him, Hardwick begins to see red. This bastard f*ck, this snake from hell, has shot and killed his colleague, his closest friend, their leader.

Brooke must pay.

Hardwick pulls out his handgun and fires at the door. He kicks it down, and rushes towards Brooke, who is standing in front of his office desk with his own gun out. Before he can shoot down Hardwick, Brooke is tackled and forced onto the table with Hardwick's gun pressed against the temple of his head.

"I'm going to f*ck you up like you f*cked up Mike, you absolute sh*tc*nt!" Hardwick screams, tears welling up in his eyes as his anger continues to simmer and boil over.

Brooke stares up at Hardwick's enraged face. His face doesn't show a single ounce of emotion. "Do it."

Hardwick tries to pull the trigger, but his grip falters. His index finger refuses to bend; it is as if his entire body is fighting against his will.

"I know that for one thing, whatever you're feeling right now is not genuine."

"Don't go there, Brooke. You don't know..."

"I do know. I know for a fact that the government has tampered with you. You are not feeling anything real and any connection you have with those people outside is simply a manufactured lie."

"Shut up!" Hardwick presses the gun closer to Brooke's head.

"You're not a real person, Hardwick. Neither is Mike. Get that through your sh*tass brain and get off me, you mindless drone."

"SHUT UP! YOU DON'T KNOW SH*T, BROOKE!" Hardwick tries to pull the trigger again, but his finger locks up.

"Keep on telling yourself that, Hardwick. If you were a real person, you would have shot me by now."

"Go on. Prove to me that you have agency. Prove to yourself that you're real. Shoot me."

Hardwick's finger begins to bend ever so slightly, but before it gets a chance to give way, a sharp pain shoots through the back of his head, and his vision goes dark.

...

"Thanks, Gordon." Josh Heeler shakes the hand of the dinghy operator and steps off onto the port. It is currently 5:05pm.

As he walks to his car, an irritating pain, the blunt and throbbing kind that tells you "hey, you need to take care of this, idiot" irradiates from the base of his skull. He's not exactly sure how or why his head hurts in that particular area. Perhaps he slept awkwardly or some moronic recruit accidentally whacked him across the head?

He approaches his car, and notices a small note has been tucked in the windshield wiper. He picks it up and reads it.

[i]Dear Corporal,

During today's joint training exercise on Harriet Island with WNE Dead Ringer, a demonstration on the buttstroke technique went wrong and resulted in you getting rendered unconscious. First aid was administered and medical teams are happy to confirm that no severe harm has come to your cognitive functions or your person.

You have been given permission to rest the whole day tomorrow. Please report back to the Dreemurr Barracks by 2130 hours and inform your section commander when appropriate to do so. If any further complications arise, dial the base medical team as soon as possible.[/i]

"No wonder why I don't remember anything. Huh." Josh tucks the note away in his pocket and gets into his vehicle, before driving off. 

He leaves Newcastle Port at 5:10pm, just as the dinghy arrives back with a new soldier to drop off.
